title: Typed output contract observer and automated mitigation for staged traffic
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight, production-safe contract observer that runs alongside our rollout orchestrator and verifies typed/structured outputs and function-call surfaces during canary, A/B, and shadow experiments. The observer will combine strict schema validation with a semantic delta scorer for function-call arguments/return values. Goals: detect breaking changes to call surfaces or payload shape, surface interpretable diffs to engineers and PMs, and enable configurable automated mitigation actions (pause, alert, soft-fail, auto-rollback) with hysteresis to avoid noisy flips.
acceptance_criteria: Observer ingests mirrored & canary traffic and produces per-request 'contract_divergence' metric (0.0-1.0)
Schema validation rules can be loaded per-model or per-route and applied in shadow/canary without impacting production latency
Auto-mitigation workflow: if 5% of canary requests exceed threshold X for T minutes, the rollout is paused and an incident is created with a prefilled triage checklist
Console dashboard shows 1h/24h/7d views: divergence rate, top schema violations, top mismatched function names and argument diffs
False positive rate < 5% on a held-out dataset of known non-breaking payload variations
Integration tests cover syntactic diffs, semantic diffs (via embeddings), and hysteresis/unwind behavior
notes_and_updates: 2025-02-10 - Scoped MVP: schema validator + simple signature diff + alerting hook. Decided to defer advanced automated safe-fallback (e.g., runtime type coercion) to later phase.

2025-02-14 - Spike summary: compared two approaches for semantic diffs: token-level edit distance (fast) vs embedding cosine similarity on serialized JSON (slower but handles reordering). Picked hybrid: syntactic checks first, embeddings for 'semantic' argument equivalence when types are complex. Details: doc/confluence/typed-output-observer-spike (internal).

2025-02-20 - Design review w/ PM & DX: added requirement for per-customer policy overrides (customers can set stricter thresholds), and retention policy for violation samples (30 days). UX: Console should allow quick rollback from the violation pivot with one click.

2025-02-24 - Implementation: started implementation of schema rule loader (YAML schema per route). Core components: validator service (go), delta scorer (python microservice using small-vectorstore + faiss), sink to telemetry (metrics 'output.schema.divergence', 'toolcall.abi.change_count').

2025-02-26 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/8345 - initial schema validator + unit tests. QA flagged race condition when loading updated schemas during active canaries. Added locking and incremental reload. Assigned to @owen-patel for fix.

2025-03-01 - Integration test: deployed to staging for small canary (1% traffic). Observed 0.9% divergence rate on control; tuned threshold to 0.12. Kept auto-rollback disabled for this run; collecting samples.

2025-03-02 - Roadblock: embedding scorer latencies spike under high QPS in staging. Proposal: add sampling and async scoring; syntactic violations keep immediate critical flagging. Action: implement async scorer + backpressure (ETA 3 days).
implementation_plan: 1) Build schema rule format + validator library (go) and expose schema management API
2) Add request mirroring hook in rollout proxy to forward a copy to observer (no sync path impact)
3) Implement delta scorer service (python). Use fast syntactic checks first; fallback to embeddings for deep checks
4) Telemetry: emit 'contract_divergence' (gauge), 'contract_violation_count' (counter), 'toolcall_name_mismatch' (counter), tag by model, route, canary_id
5) Console: add widget for active canary contract health and per-violation drilldown with example payloads and suggested mitigation
6) Automation: create mitigation playbook with policies (pause, alert, auto-rollback) with hysteresis and manual approvals for P1 customers
7) Run staged rollout in staging -> limited canary -> canary with auto-mitigation off -> enable auto-mitigation for low-risk models
risks_and_tradeoffs: Latency: embedding-based semantic checks can be expensive under high QPS. Mitigation: sample requests and async scoring; ensure syntactic checks catch most regressions synchronously.
False positives: overly strict schemas can block intended benign transformations. Mitigation: provide 'soft-fail' mode and a learning window where queries are logged but not blocked.
Data retention/privacy: storing samples for diagnostics may contain PII. Mitigation: scan-and-redact pipeline and per-customer retention policies.
Operational complexity: adding another pipeline increases SRE burden. Mitigation: keep observer read-only for first release; provide clear runbooks and alert thresholds.
